equation_request.abstract:
We consider the Unitary Permutation problem which consists, given $n$ unitary gates $U_{1},\ldots,U_{n}$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, in applying the unitary gates in the order specified by $\sigma$, i.e. in performing $U_{\sigma(n)}\circ\ldots\circ U_{\sigma(1)}$.

This problem has been introduced and investigated in [7] where two models of computations are considered. This first is the (standard) model of query complexity: the complexity measure is the number of calls to any of the unitary gates $U_{i}$ in a quantum circuit which solves the problem. The second model provides quantum switches and treats unitary transformations as inputs of second order. In that case the complexity measure is the number of quantum switches. In their paper, Colnaghi et al. [7] have shown that the problem can be solved within $n^{2}$ calls in the query model and $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ quantum switches in the new model.

We refine these results by proving that $n\log_{2}(n)+\Theta(n)$ quantum switches are necessary and sufficient to solve this problem, whereas $n^{2}-2n+4$ calls are sufficient to solve this problem in the standard quantum circuit model. We prove, with an additional assumption on the family of gates used in the circuits, that $n^{2}-o(n^{7/4+\epsilon})$ queries are required, for any $\epsilon>0$. The upper and lower bounds for the standard quantum circuit model are established by pointing out connections with the permutation as substring problem introduced by Karp.

specification.problem: Unitary Permutation: given n unitary gates U_1..U_n and a permutation sigma of {1..n}, apply the gates in the order given by sigma, i.e. implement U_{sigma(n)} o ... o U_{sigma(1)}. Complexity is measured as the number of gate calls in the standard query model, or as the number of quantum switches in the second-order model.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Complexity bounds only: upper and lower bounds on the number of quantum switches and of queries. The abstract gives no explicit circuit, so no circuit construction is reconstructed. The lower bound for queries assumes an extra restriction on the gate family.

steps.description: Take the input state on the data register and the description of sigma as the control; the sequence must realize the composition in eq_1.

Query model: realize the composition by a circuit calling the gates, with the number of calls bounded by the stated upper bound; the actual construction (via the permutation-as-substring connection) is not given in the abstract.
Switch model: realize the composition with quantum switches, using n log2(n)+Theta(n) switches; the construction is not given in the abstract.

specification.measurement: None specified in the abstract. The task is implementing a unitary (the composition in eq_1), so no measurement is part of the stated problem; any verification would measure the output data register after applying the circuit to a test state (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: None specified. The only classical input is the permutation sigma, which determines the order of application. No result decoding is described in the abstract.
